https://www.dnews.gr/eidhseis/news-in-en.text: Gross disposable income in Greece fell 2.5% from the previous quarter, according to Eurostat. Yet household spending on individual consumption rose 1.2% over the same period. Greek households entered 2026 under growing financial strain, diverging sharply from broader European trends as falling incomes forced many families to dip into savings while cutting back on long-term investment. New figures from Eurostat for the first quarter of 2026 show that, while household finances across the European Union and the eurozone remained broadly stable, Greece stood out for the deterioration in its domestic picture. Disposable incomes declined, consumer spending continued to rise, and both savings and investment weakened markedly, suggesting that households are increasingly relying on accumulated financial buffers to maintain day-to-day consumption. Gross disposable income in Greece fell 2.5% from the previous quarter, according to Eurostat. Yet household spending on individual consumption rose 1.2% over the same period, indicating that families continued to spend more despite having less income available. The gap underscores the growing pressure on household budgets as higher living costs and weaker purchasing power leave consumers with fewer options than drawing down savings. Greece recorded the second-largest decline in the household saving rate among EU member states, with the indicator falling by 3.7 percentage points from the previous quarter. Only Romania posted a steeper decline, at 5.3 percentage points, while Hungary recorded the strongest improvement, with its saving rate rising by 3.4 percentage points. Household investment also deteriorated sharply. Gross fixed capital formation—primarily spending on home purchases, construction and renovations—fell 11.8%, the steepest decline among all countries covered by the Eurostat report. Greece also recorded the largest drop in the household investment rate in the EU, down 0.7 percentage points from the previous quarter. Across the European Union, household disposable income increased 0.9% in the first quarter, while consumption rose 0.6% and household investment edged down just 0.5%. In the eurozone, disposable income increased 0.7%, consumption expanded 0.8%, and investment also slipped only marginally, by 0.5%. Broader European indicators point to a far more resilient consumer sector. Real income per capita was unchanged in the eurozone after rising 0.2% in the previous quarter, while it increased 0.1% across the EU. Real consumption per capita remained flat in the eurozone and declined only 0.2% in the EU as a whole. Eurostat attributed the resilience of household incomes across Europe largely to higher employee compensation and increased social benefits. Those gains were partly offset by lower net property income, current transfers, taxes and social contributions, which limited overall income growth. Savings trends further illustrate the divergence. The household saving rate was unchanged in the eurozone and increased by 0.2 percentage points across the EU, suggesting that many European households continue to build financial buffers despite persistent economic uncertainty. Greece moved in the opposite direction. The sharp decline in savings suggests that a growing number of households are either drawing down accumulated reserves or are no longer able to set aside money, highlighting the increasing pressure on family finances even as much of Europe experiences relative stability. https://www.coventrytelegraph.net/news/c.text: A Latvian man charged over the death of a 12-year-old Coventry boy in a hit-and-run has been remanded in custody after being extradited to the UK. Dolars Aleksanders appeared at Birmingham Magistrates' Court today (August 6). Aleksanders, 23, is charged with causing the death of Keaton Slater by dangerous driving in Radford in June 2024. He spoke only to confirm his identity and date of birth during the three-minute hearing. District Judge David Wain was told Aleksanders is alleged to have been driving a black BMW when he caused the fatal collision on June 14, 2024. He was remanded to appear at Birmingham Crown Court on September 3. Aleksanders, who was detained in Latvia in July, was flown to Gatwick Airport on Wednesday. Ben Samples, from the CPS, said: “We have decided to charge Dolars Aleksanders with one count of causing death by dangerous driving following a police investigation into a fatal road traffic collision that led to the death of Keaton Slater. Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court to pursue criminal proceedings. “CPS West Midlands has worked closely with West Midlands Police , Home Office, the Latvian authorities, Europol, the Joint International Crime Centre (JICC), CPS International, and our Extradition Unit to bring Mr Aleksanders back to face proceedings in a UK court for an alleged crime that took place here.” Sign up for CoventryLive newsletters to stay up to date with the latest news across Coventry and Warwickshire . https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text: Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, will ring the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange when the company’s shares begin trading. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, will ring the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange when the company’s shares begin trading. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images Anthropic Anthropic sets share price at $83 for stock market debut, above expected range Artificial intelligence firm positioned for one of the biggest IPOs in history, with trading slated to begin Thursday Dara Kerr Wed 18 Nov 2026 16.39 EST Last modified on Wed 18 Nov 2026 18.44 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Anthropic set the share price for its debut on the US stock market at $83 on Wednesday, positioning the artificial intelligence company for one of the biggest initial public offerings in history. The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with CEO Dario Amodei and other co-founders ringing the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange. The pricing is above Anthropic’s earlier estimates. Last week, the San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, set its preliminary share price at $70 to $78. With all shares counted, those prices put Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO) from $1.26tn to $1.41tn. Elon Musk’s SpaceX debuted on Wall Street in June with the biggest market offering ever at $1.77tn. With Anthropic setting its share price at $83, it could now surpass SpaceX. Amodei is planning to sell about $260m worth of shares with the IPO, as are his six fellow co-founders. At the top of the price range, the co-founders’ stakes will be worth more than $18bn each. When Anthropic filed for its IPO last month, the company detailed rapidly rising revenue in its prospectus: $41m in 2023, $386m in 2024, $4.585bn in 2025 (an increase of more than 1,000%), then $16.286bn in the first six months of 2026 alone. The company disclosed that, as of the end of June, it had raised $141.1bn. Despite the increasing revenue, Anthropic disclosed a net loss of $80bn for the first half of 2026. Anthropic’s main expenditure listed in its investor prospectus is computing power from datacenters. The company has compute purchase commitments and lease agreements of more than $70bn over the next 12 months and more than $450bn by 2030, with a further $450bn due by 2045. Anthropic is the first company at the forefront of the generative AI boom to go public, and its performance is likely to affect investors’ enthusiasm. Its competitor OpenAI was slated to hit Wall Street later this year, but CEO Sam Altman has said that the company opted to delay its IPO until it can overcome safety concerns. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to TechScape A weekly dive in to how technology is shaping our lives after newsletter promotion Anthropic’s IPO comes during a volatile time for AI and the stock market. Last month, the industry saw a broader slowdown, with share prices dropping at several companies amid growing concern about the technology. Then, last week, Nvidia, which designs the chips AI companies use to power their chatbots, was racked with a scandal that led to CEO Jensen Huang resigning after reports of multiple extramarital affairs. https://hotnews.ro/trump-evita-sa-discut.text: Președintele american Donald Trump a declarat vineri că el și liderul rus Vladimir Putin au purtat discuții foarte constructive privind Ucraina în cadrul întâlnirii lor din China, dar a adăugat că nu dorește să discute despre garanții de securitate pentru Kiev fără un acord de pace mai amplu. „Avem discuții foarte bune. Cred că există șanse reale să reușim”, a declarat Trump în cadrul unei conferințe de presă la Casa Albă, după călătoria lui în Asia, unde s-a întâlnit cu Putin și cu președintele chinez Xi Jinping, în cadrul unui summit fără precedent. Trump a discutat cu Putin, pe care l-a numit „prieten”, în cadrul reuniunii Cooperării Economice Asia-Pacific (APEC) de la Shenzhen, China, care a avut loc săptămâna aceasta. „El și-a exprimat clar dorința ca războiul dintre Rusia și Ucraina să se încheie pe cale diplomatică. Și am vorbit cu reprezentanții noștri, care fac o treabă bună, dar este o sarcină dificilă”, a spus Trump, potrivit Reuters. Trump a lăsat deoparte subiectul garanțiilor de securitate pentru Ucraina, care reprezintă de mult timp un punct sensibil în negocieri, afirmând: „Nu vreau să vorbesc despre garanții de securitate, deoarece trebuie mai întâi să ajungem la un acord”. Jared Kushner, consilierul și ginerele lui Trump, a declarat joi, după discuțiile privind Ucraina de la Berlin, că Trump este deschis la ideea de a oferi Ucrainei garanții de securitate similare celor prevăzute în articolul 5 al NATO, care stabilesc că un atac asupra unui membru este un atac asupra tuturor. Kushner a mai afirmat că, în opinia lui, negociatorii americani au reușit să-i facă pe ruși „să se simtă confortabili cu această idee”. „Din perspectiva Statelor Unite, acordarea unei garanții de securitate similare cu cea prevăzută în Articolul 5 (din Tratatul Atlanticului de Nord) este o decizie cu adevărat, cu adevărat importantă”, a declarat Kushner într-o conferință de presă după ce a participat, alături de Steve Witkoff, la o reuniune a aliaților Kievului. „Cred că președintele Trump este deschis acestei idei, dar este evident că aceasta trebuie să servească intereselor Statelor Unite”, a adăugat el. „Acesta este un pas înainte semnificativ pe care l-am realizat și cred că am reușit să-i convingem pe ruși de acest concept, conform căruia orice garanție de securitate pentru Ucraina s-ar baza pe Articolul 5, piatra de temelie a apărării colective a NATO”, a subliniat Kushner. Cu toate acestea, viceministrul rus de Externe, Serghei Riabkov, a respins vineri această idee și a declarat că orice formă de „cvasi-aderare” a Kievului la alianța militară occidentală este total inacceptabilă pentru Moscova, potrivit presei de stat ruse. „Aș dori să spun că până și simpla idee a unei formule de cvasi-aderare a Ucrainei la NATO, precum și căutarea unei așa-zise – între ghilimele – «soluții creative» în acest domeniu reprezintă o opțiune inacceptabilă pentru noi. Discutăm despre garanțiile de securitate, înainte de toate, din perspectiva asigurării securității propriei noastre țări”, a fost citat Riabkov de agenția de presă Interfax. El a făcut comentariile după ce a fost întrebat dacă garanțiile pentru Ucraina de tipul celor prevăzute de Articolul 5 al NATO ar fi acceptabile pentru Rusia. „În ceea ce privește Ucraina, lăsați-i să recunoască natura irevocabilă a cererii noastre ca acest stat să nu adere la NATO. Când acest lucru se va întâmpla, cred că problema garanțiilor de securitate va putea fi discutată într-un fel sau altul”, a adăugat Riabkov, potrivit aceleiași agenții de presă a statului rus. Riabkov a confirmat de asemenea că se lucrează la organizarea unei posibile vizite la Moscova a unor reprezentanți ai Marii Britanii, Germaniei și Franței. Vladimir Putin a declarat joi că Moscova a propus ca emisarii europeni să se deplaseze în Rusia pentru a-și clarifica poziția cu privire la negocierile de pace privind Ucraina, înainte de a se decide formatul viitoarelor discuții. Întrebat despre această discrepanță, Trump a pus-o pe seama tacticilor de negociere. „Uitați, partea noastră face anumite declarații pentru că este și un război de relații publice. Noi vom spune anumite lucruri, iar ei vor spune altele”, a spus președintele american. „Vă pot spune doar că președintele Putin ar dori să se rezolve această problemă, și asta este sigur”, a continuat Trump. Invazia Rusiei în Ucraina din februarie 2022 a dus la cel mai sângeros conflict din Europa de după cel de-al Doilea Război Mondial. La câteva ore după ce Trump, Xi și Putin au emis „o declarație de pace” în urma întâlnirii lor din China, Rusia a lansat vineri unul dintre cele mai ample atacuri cu rachete și drone din timpul războiului din Ucraina, lovind facilități electrice și ucigând opt persoane.
